beats.text: Move forty thousand dollars of pension on paper, and this retired couple pays about three thousand four hundred dollars less tax a year.
Pat, sixty-six: a hundred thousand dollars, mostly an eighty thousand dollar workplace pension. Jo, sixty-six: twenty thousand.
Pat can report up to half of that pension on Jo's return. Forty thousand moves. Both land at sixty thousand: about three thousand and thirty dollars less tax in Manitoba.
And Jo can now claim the pension credit: three hundred and eighty-eight dollars more.
But CPP and OAS can't be split. And under sixty-five, RRIF withdrawals don't count. A workplace life pension does.
The twist: no money moves. The cheque still goes to Pat. It's form T ten thirty-two, filed with both returns, every year.
Next: the disability tax credit. Follow so you don't miss it.
